newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses resume slide as Wall St declines.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses resume slide as Wall St declines.

text.p: European stock markets traded sharply lower on Monday, stung by Wall Street stocks resuming their slide after Friday's 148 point slump.
European shares, which had been nervously waiting to see which way the Dow would jump, immediately turned lower again, having early recouped some of their opening losses.
The dollar was firm despite a warning by Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka that Japan would act decisively against excessive currency movements which failed to have much impact in Europe.

Analysts said stock and bond markets faced a stern test this week, U.S. markets are likely to be volatile with key inflation figures due on Tuesday and a series of earnings figures from major high technology companies.
The first of those earnings figures were due to come from chip leader Intel after American markets closed.
European bond markets steadied after an early dip, with British gilts perking up following figures showing UK producer prices fell 0.1 percent in March.
Investor focus remained fixed firmly on the United States, however, with the first major test on Tuesday when the U.S. government will report March retail inflation.

Although economic data has so far shown robust growth and subdued inflation, a stronger than expected consumer inflation figure after Friday's producer price index rise could underline the threat of rising interest rates.
Many market watchers already expect the Federal Reserve's policy-making open market committee to raise rates again when it meets next month.

First-quarter earnings reports due from a number of other major U.S. companies, such as Microsoft and General Motors, might also weigh on investors contemplating the prospect that the Dow could fall another five percent on top of its 10 percent decline from record levels in March.
Wall Street's tumble had an immediate impact on major European markets, with the blue chip indices in both Paris and Frankfurt dropping more than two percent at the start.
Among second tier bourses, the Stockholm, Amsterdam and Madrid markets suffered sharp falls, but Milan's all share MIBTEL index recovered its losses to show a modest gain.
London slipped anew as Wall Street's decline deepened in early trading.
A firmer bond market and benign set of producer price inflation numbers earlier provided some support but traders said interest rate worries hurt sentiment.
By 1415 GMT the blue chip FTSE 100 index was showing a decline of 0.6 percent to 4,244.7, with technical analysts seeing the next support level at 4,220.
Germany's DAX index closed floor trade nearly two percent lower after a mid-session rebound never really gained ground.
The stronger dollar and a steady, slightly firmer Bund market lent some support but dealers said the market was vulnerable to further losses.
The DAX closed 60.15 points, 1.80 percent, down at 3,279.90 after earlier hitting a day-low of 3,266.96. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index was down nearly 40 points at 3,279.

Very few stocks managed to buck the downward trend. Auto components maker Kolbenschmidt AG firmed 1.20 marks to 29.90 after the Berlin cartel office approved a majority stake in it by the defence and engineering group Rheinmetall.
In Paris, the CAC-40 index briefly narrowed its losses after tumbling more than two percent at the start but turned down once more with Wall Street.
The blue-chip index, which lost 1.28 percent on Friday, was standing 0.61 percent down at 2,558 points by 1415 GMT after bouncing off a low of 2,528.30 points.
The dollar was holding steady above 1.72 marks and around 126.40 yen with dealers keeping a close eye on the Dow.

Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London, saw more upside potential in dollar/mark as Japan's threat of intervention was likely to provide some resistance to the dollar against the yen.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7216 marks and 126.34 yen compared with 1.7255 marks and 126.15 yen in late European trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 26.1 points, or 0.61 percent, at 4,244.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 16.31 points, or 0.63 percent, at 2,558.25.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 60.15 points, or 1.8 percent, at 3,279.47. In later screen trade the IBIS DAX was down 1.2 percent at 3,279.47.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed lower at $346.65 from Friday's $347.95. Silver was quoted five cents lower at $4.74.
